foundBy: MT-03, MT-05 (charter run on staging)
title: A refresh cut off after the server rotated the token logs the user out on every device
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in on staging.
2. Open /bot and, as soon as its start-up POST /api/auth/refresh is sent, navigate to /transactions (or reload, or lose the network).
3. The next page load sends the old refresh cookie.
expected: A refresh whose answer was lost (navigation, reload, flaky network) does not end the session; only a real token reuse (a stolen copy) revokes every session.
actual: The server already rotated the token, so the old cookie is treated as theft: 401, and every session of the user is revoked, including a second device that did nothing. Seen 3 times during the charter run on an unstable network.
rootCause: server/src/services/auth.js refresh(): any reuse of a rotated token revokes all sessions (docs/04 §4.3 'Reuse detection'), with no grace window for a lost response.
fix: Approved by the student on 2026-11-21 ("Yes, 30 s grace"). refresh() in server/src/services/auth.js now gives reuse a 30 s grace window: a rotated token that comes back within 30 s while its replacement has never been refreshed is a lost answer, so the unused replacement is revoked and the token is rotated once more (both old rows point at the new session). Any other reuse still revokes every session. docs/04 §4.3 updated.
evidence: charter-runs/2026-11-21/BUG-refresh-abort.mp4, BUG-refresh-abort.log, repro-refresh-abort.mjs, MT-03.attempt1.mp4 (local, git-ignored) ; retest on staging with the fix deployed, same repro script: charter-runs/2026-11-21/retest-T21/ (BUG-003-retest.mp4, .log): the next refresh answers 200, the user stays on /transactions, the untouched second device refreshes 200

foundBy: Code review S2 of PR #47 (T21)
title: A refresh running in parallel with "revoke every session" keeps its new session alive
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in, refresh A → B.
2. Within 30 s send two refreshes with A at the same moment (or a reuse of A in parallel with a refresh of B).
3. Count the user's active sessions.
expected: One request is treated as theft, so every session of the user is revoked and none stays active.
actual: The winner's new session stays active after the "revoke all" (about 3 runs in 5 in the reviewer's repro).
rootCause: revokeAllSessions is one updateMany on revokedAt: null. A parallel refresh that had already claimed its old session called openSession() after that updateMany had passed, so its new row was never matched (server/src/services/sessions.js, auth.js rotate()).
fix: revokeAllSessions first stamps users.sessionsRevokedAt, then revokes. Every session carries chainStartedAt (the time of the login that began its rotation chain, copied forward on each rotation). rotate() re-reads the stamp and status after openSession(); if the stamp is not older than the chain's login, it revokes the new session and answers 401 INVALID_REFRESH (403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED after an admin lock). Comparing with the chain's login rather than the newest session also closes the gap the PR #50 review found: a session created while the stamp was being written is younger than the stamp, but its chain is not.
evidence: TC-F1-20 (4 cases): pausing Session.create makes the interleaving deterministic; the 2 interleaving cases failed before the fix (200, one session alive), and the 'session younger than the stamp' case failed against the first version of the fix (200). All pass now; 40 real parallel retries left 0 active sessions.

foundBy: manual: deploy check 2026-11-21
title: bot-e2e.mjs --help (or any unknown option) crashes with a stack trace instead of printing the usage
stepsToReproduce:
1. node tools/bot-e2e/bot-e2e.mjs --help
2. node tools/bot-e2e/bot-e2e.mjs list --targt staging
expected: --help/-h prints the usage and exits 0; an unknown option prints a one-line error plus the usage and exits 1, like an unknown command.
actual: Both print an uncaught TypeError [ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION] with a Node stack trace and no usage.
rootCause: parseArgs() runs in strict mode (the default), so it throws on any option it was not told about; the tool declared no help option and did not catch the error. Only unknown commands had a friendly path.
fix: Declare --help/-h; catch parseArgs's ERR_PARSE_ARGS_* errors (unknown option, missing value) and print the message on one line, then the usage, exit 1. The usage text moved into one usage() function shared by --help, the help command and both error paths.
evidence: TC-NF-15 (4 cases, node --test tools/bot-e2e/bot-e2e.test.mjs): all 4 failed before the fix (stack trace, exit 1 for --help) and pass after it.

foundBy: X4 bots & receipts charter (round 2, staging), finding X4#1
title: Confirming a stale Bot inbox card silently rewrites a transaction that was already saved from the chat
stepsToReproduce:
1. Link a Telegram chat and send 'bún chả 40k' (a draft appears).
2. Open Hộp thư bot and leave it open.
3. Press ✅ in the chat: the transaction is confirmed at 40.000.
4. On the open page change the stale card's amount to 99k and press Xác nhận.
expected: The 409 ALREADY_CONFIRMED refusal changes nothing: the saved transaction stays at 40.000 (docs/04 §4.4).
actual: PATCH /api/transactions/:id answers 200, then /confirm answers 409. The UI says 'Giao dịch này đã được xác nhận.' and drops the card, but the saved transaction now has amount 99.000. The money changed without the user being told.
rootCause: DraftCard.tsx confirm() sent an unconditional PATCH with the edits before POST /confirm. PATCH edits any non-deleted transaction (the Transactions page needs that), so the edit was written before confirmTransaction saw status 'confirmed' and answered 409. The card was stale because the BUG-004 fix only reloads the list when the inbox opens.
fix: POST /transactions/:id/confirm now takes the same optional fields as PATCH and saves edits and status in one Transaction.findOneAndUpdate({ _id, userId, status: 'draft', deletedAt: null }); if it matches nothing the answer is 409 and nothing was written. DraftCard sends its edits with the confirm and no longer sends a separate PATCH. Plain PATCH still edits confirmed transactions.

foundBy: X1 auth & security charter (round 2, staging), finding X1#1
title: Password is only checked on its first 72 bytes: with Vietnamese letters, a different password (or just a prefix) logs in and can change the password
stepsToReproduce:
1. POST /api/auth/register with password 'ư'×36 + 'a1b2c3d4e5f6' (48 characters, 84 UTF-8 bytes).
2. POST /api/auth/login with 'ư'×36 + 'totally-different'.
3. POST /api/auth/login with 'ư'×36 alone.
4. PATCH /api/users/me/password with a wrong currentPassword that shares the first 72 bytes.
expected: Login succeeds only with the exact password the user set (docs/04 §4.3, §4.10). A password bcrypt would truncate is rejected with 400.
actual: Register accepts the 84-byte password (201). Steps 2 and 3 log in (200), and step 4 changes the password with a wrong current password (204).
rootCause: server/src/routes/auth.js `newPassword = z.string().min(8).max(72)` counts UTF-16 characters, not UTF-8 bytes. bcryptjs silently uses only the first 72 bytes, so every byte after that is ignored. The same schema serves register and change-password, and the client forms copied the character count.
fix: The shared newPassword schema refines on Buffer.byteLength(p, 'utf8') <= 72, which covers register and change-password. The register and Settings forms check the same rule with TextEncoder, and the hint states the limit.

foundBy: X5 admin & preferences charter (round 2, staging), finding X5#1
title: 'Log out other devices' (and password change, single-device logout) leaves a device logged in if it refreshes at the same moment
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in twice through the API: device A and device B.
2. From A send DELETE /api/sessions?others=true; send B's POST /api/auth/refresh 0–25 ms later.
3. If B's refresh answered 200, refresh B again with the new cookie and list GET /api/sessions as A.
expected: After 'Log out other devices' or a password change no other device keeps a working session, as BUG-006 guaranteed for revoke-all (docs/04 §4.3–4.4).
actual: In 6 of 12 trials B's overlapping refresh answered 200, its next refresh also answered 200, and A's session list showed B as an active device.
rootCause: server/src/services/sessions.js revokeOtherSessions() only ran Session.updateMany({ revokedAt: null, _id: { $ne: keep } }). Unlike revokeAllSessions it did not stamp users.sessionsRevokedAt first, which is the only thing rotate()'s late re-check reads. A refresh that had already claimed its old session inserted its new session after the updateMany and nothing revoked it. Logout and DELETE /sessions/:id had the same gap.
fix: revokeOtherSessions moves the kept session's chainStartedAt 1 ms past now, stamps users.sessionsRevokedAt, then revokes the others, so the BUG-006 re-check in rotate() kills a late new session; revokeAllSessions is the same function with no kept session. Logout and DELETE /sessions/:id use endSessionChain(): every row of that device's chain gets chainEndedAt before its live row is revoked, and rotate() re-reads the rows it claimed.

foundBy: X1 auth & security charter (round 2, staging), finding X1#3
title: After an admin lock, refresh answers 401 INVALID_REFRESH instead of 403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED, so the locked user is silently sent to the login page
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in a fresh account on 3 devices.
2. As admin: PATCH /api/admin/users/<id> {status:'locked'}.
3. POST /api/auth/refresh with each device's cookie; reload the user's open tab.
expected: docs/04 §4.3 'Lock user (admin)': login and refresh return 403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED, and the user learns the account is locked.
actual: All 3 refreshes answer 401 INVALID_REFRESH; only login answers 403. The reloaded tab lands on /login with no message.
rootCause: The admin lock revokes every session, so refresh() in server/src/services/auth.js never reached its status check: the claim needs revokedAt: null, and a revoked token fell into the invalid/theft branches (401). The only accountLocked() for refresh was in rotate(), which a live session alone reaches. TC-F11-02 asserted the 401. On the client, refreshSession dropped the error code.
fix: refresh() loads the owner's status for any stored token that is no longer live and throws accountLocked() before the reuse/theft branch (unknown tokens still get 401). refreshSession remembers an ACCOUNT_LOCKED failure and LoginPage shows the locked message. TC-F11-02 now expects 403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED, per docs/04 §4.3.

foundBy: X2 money & data charter (round 2, staging), finding X2#1
title: Archiving the default wallet keeps it as the default: quick add, the Add form, bot and receipt drafts keep filing new money into a hidden wallet, while Settings shows 'Không chọn'
stepsToReproduce:
1. Fresh account (default wallet Tiền mặt).
2. /wallets → archive Tiền mặt.
3. /transactions → quick add 'phở 45k'.
4. Click Thêm giao dịch.
5. Open /settings.
expected: docs/03 §3.3: an archived wallet is hidden from pickers. Archiving the default clears it (as deleting does), so new entries go to an active wallet and Settings agrees with the server.
actual: The quick-add chip shows the archived Tiền mặt and Enter saves into it; the Add form preselects it; POST /transactions/parse returns the archived default; Settings → Ví mặc định shows 'Không chọn'. Bot and receipt drafts do the same.
rootCause: server/src/services/wallets.js updateWallet() applied {archived: true} without touching users.defaultWalletId (deleteWallet does clear it), and every reader (parser fallback, receipts, TransactionDialog) trusted defaultWalletId without checking archived.

foundBy: X3 UI, i18n & a11y charter (round 2, staging), finding X3#3
title: Dashboard chart adds 6 keyboard stops with no name and no visible focus (svg role=application plus 5 SVG <g> layers), in Chromium-based browsers
stepsToReproduce:
1. Log in and open the dashboard (≥ md).
2. Focus main, then Tab past the Spending/Income switch.
3. Watch the focus.
expected: Keyboard users go from the switch to 'See all'; every stop has a name (WCAG 4.1.2) and a visible focus ring (WCAG 2.4.7). The chart's text summary is its accessible alternative (docs/05 §5.8).
actual: Six extra Tab stops: the recharts svg (role=application, empty <title>) and 5 <g class=recharts-zIndex-layer_*> nodes with no role or name; none shows a focus ring. axe does not flag them.
rootCause: recharts 3.11's accessibilityLayer makes the svg a stop. Its ZIndexPortal renders bare <g> layers that React portals into; React attaches focus listeners to each portal container, and Chromium makes an SVG element with a focus listener sequentially focusable (shown with CDP getEventListeners and a control <g>).
fix: accessibilityLayer={false} removes the svg stop. useNoTabStops sets tabindex=-1 on the zIndex layers, and a MutationObserver reapplies it when recharts re-creates them; the mouse tooltip still works (inert would block it). The figcaption summary stays.

title: A multi-line bot message makes a draft only for line 1 when the reply to line 1 fails; the other lines are lost
stepsToReproduce:

foundBy: Recorded retest of BUG-018 on staging (round 2), then reproduced in the real Zalo chat on production
title: The bot / quick-add parser accepts amounts over the 10^13 ceiling: the line previews as valid and fails to save, and in the bot one such line loses every line of the message
stepsToReproduce:
1. POST /api/transactions/parse {"text": "cafe 20000000000000\ncafe 45k"}.
2. Save the first draft with POST /api/transactions.
3. In the real Zalo chat on production send 'xang 20000000000000' / 'cafe 25k' in one message.
expected: A line whose amount is over 10^13 counts as a line without a readable amount: quick add names it and does not save it, the bot says it could not read that line, and the other lines still work.
actual: /parse answers 200 with amount 20000000000000 (the chip shows 20.000.000.000.000 ₫) and the save answers 400 too_big. In the real Zalo chat the bot sent no reply at all and the valid 'cafe 25k' line was lost too (no draft): the over-cap line hit the Transaction model validator and took the whole message down. Raised to S2 Major after the production repro.
rootCause: server/src/bot/parser.js accepted any positive safe integer, not only amounts up to MAX_MONEY, so the parser shared by the bots, /transactions/parse and quick add let over-cap amounts through to the model validator, which threw inside createDrafts.
fix: parser.js checked() is the one place every caller's amount goes through; it now accepts 1 … MAX_MONEY (imported from models/Transaction.js), so an over-cap line becomes null and is listed in noAmountLines like 'cafe' with no number. createDrafts saves the good lines and then sends noAmountLines ('⚠️ Chưa ghi dòng 1: không đọc được số tiền (tối đa 10.000.000.000.000 ₫) …').

foundBy: Card-check agents re-running the parser on main bfa6f57 while drafting the assistant cards (§2.11.1 time phrases)
title: A year or month typed before the amount is saved as the amount ('thuê nhà năm 2026 36tr' → 2.026 ₫)
stepsToReproduce:
1. POST /api/transactions/parse {"text": "thuê nhà năm 2026 36tr"} (also 'học phí năm 2025 12.000.000', 'ăn tối tháng 10 50').
2. Or type the same line in web quick add and press Enter.
3. Or send it to the bot.
expected: 36.000.000 ₫ (12.000.000, 50.000); the year or month stays in the note. A line whose only number is such a date has no amount and saves nothing.
actual: 2.026 ₫ / 2.025 ₫ / 10.000 ₫. Quick add saved it as a confirmed transaction; the bot saved a draft. Written the other way round ('36tr năm 2026') it was right.
rootCause: findAmount in server/src/bot/parser.js took the first number that was not a bare guess; a 4-digit year counted as one, and nothing treated 'năm YYYY' or 'tháng M' as a date.
fix: findAmount skips a bare number right after nam/năm that is a year 1900–2099, or after tháng/thang that is 1–12, unless it carries a money unit or thousands separators. A date-only line has no amount (noAmountLines / 422 NO_AMOUNT_FOUND / the bot's help text). One fix in the parser every entry point uses.

foundBy: Card-check agents with a deterministic test pausing bcrypt.compare inside login on main bfa6f57
title: A login with the old password that overlaps a password change keeps a working session
stepsToReproduce:
1. Device B starts POST /api/auth/login with the current password.
2. While B's bcrypt check runs, device A changes the password (PATCH /api/users/me/password, 204).
3. B's login finishes.
expected: B's login answers 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS (403 ACCOUNT_LOCKED after an admin lock) and holds no session; A stays signed in.
actual: B's login answered 200 and its session kept refreshing and calling authenticated routes after the password change.
rootCause: login() in server/src/services/auth.js read passwordHash once, awaited bcrypt, then opened its session after the change had already revoked other sessions. The BUG-006/BUG-010 re-check existed only in refresh rotation.
fix: login() re-reads the user right after openSession(); if the password hash differs from the one bcrypt checked it revokes the new session and answers 401, if the account is now locked 403. Compares the hash, not sessionsRevokedAt, so 'log out other devices' (password still valid) is unaffected.
filesOrCommit: server/src/services/auth.js, docs/04 §4.3; T78 (#78), PR #125, merged as d23e533
evidence: found: deterministic automated test on main bfa6f57 (no video) ; fix: https://github.com/dangnguyenducanh/Zalo-Tele-intergrated-financial-apps/pull/125 ; retest on staging with the fix deployed: charter-runs/2026-11-26/retest-BUG-039-040/run.log (race probe at 0/60/120/200 ms: the 0 ms overlap got 401, later logins' sessions were revoked, refresh 401)

foundBy: Live receipt upload failing on staging and production
title: Receipt reading is down on both live sites when the KIE quick tunnel's address changes or expires
stepsToReproduce:
1. Upload a receipt photo on /bot (staging or production).
2. Check KIE_PUBLIC_URL/health.
expected: A draft with the payable total (fixture mcocr khrvg → 116.000).
actual: The upload fails because the server's KIE_URL points at a trycloudflare address that no longer resolves. Happened 2026-11-25 and again overnight 2026-11-26 (tunnel process alive, address dropped).
rootCause: KIE is reached through a Cloudflare quick tunnel; its random address changes on restart and can be dropped by Cloudflare, and KIE_URL on Vercel is static.
fix: Operational each time: restart cloudflared, save the new KIE_PUBLIC_URL, push it (tools/vercel-env-push.sh) and redeploy staging then production. Permanent fix still open: a named Cloudflare tunnel with a fixed hostname (owner step).
filesOrCommit: no code change; env KIE_URL on both Vercel projects
evidence: retest after the 2026-11-26 restart: charter-runs/2026-11-26/manual-T32-receipts/receipt.mp4 (staging draft 116.000) ; recurs until a named tunnel replaces the quick tunnel
